newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Diagnostic ends consulting deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Diagnostic ends consulting deal.

text.p: U.S. Diagnostics Inc on Wednesday said it agreed to end its relationship with Coyote Consulting & Financial Services and Keith Greenberg, who served as the company's director of mergers, acquisitions and marketing.
Shareholders have brought four separate class action lawsuits against the company for allegedly failing to disclose that Keith Greenberg, one of its founders, had pleaded guilty to fraud.
But U.S. Diagnostics has denied that Greenberg was either a co-founder, officer or director of the company, saying he had worked as a consultant through Coyote.
The company said in a statement Wednesday it intended to "vigorously defend these lawsuits, although it believes it is premature to predict the ultimate outcome of the cases."

It said its board of directors had appointed a special committee of independent directors "to review the company's prior relationship with Coyote Consulting and Keith Greenberg and its prior disclosure regarding them."
The shareholders also allege that the company's stock price "declined substantially" when Greenberg's case was made public.
Earlier in the day, the company said it had agreed in principle to acquire American Shared Hospital Services in a stock swap.
